findings.description: The hop-aware companion skip in _repair_model_chain is gated on `-n "${companion_shared_hops:-}"`, i.e. on the PRIMARY chain sharing a hop with the companion chain. The repair chain is built independently (`tiny` → `claude-headless` → answering voice) and contains `claude-headless` whenever the binary is on PATH, regardless of the primary chain. In the default configuration (CONF_MODEL=gpt-5.3-codex → OpenAI family → companion `opus` → `claude-headless`; primary chain gpt-* → codex-headless) `companion_shared_hops` is empty, so the guard is false and the skip never fires even while the companion is ON `claude-headless` (phase queue/hop). The comment on the block says 'a repair never queues behind the live companion on the hop it is ON right now' — that holds only on hosts whose primary chain already ends on claude-headless (the operator's host, where the thirteenth run validated it).
findings.failure_mode: On an OpenAI-primary host with `claude` installed, every KF-004 repair's `claude-headless` hop queues behind the companion's `claude -p` for the full `_ADV_LOCK_WAIT_CLI` (CONF_TIMEOUT, 60 s default) before falling to the answering voice; up to ADV_REPAIR_MAX_PER_RUN × 60 s of the 360 s wall budget is spent waiting, and `repair_hops_skipped` stays `[]` so the envelope does not explain the latency.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `-n "${companion_shared_hops:-}"` from the guard (keep the PID/workdir/kill -0 checks) so the skip is decided purely from companion.current/companion.phase against the repair chain's own hops; add a companion-suite case with an OpenAI primary, an empty shared set and the companion parked on `claude-headless` asserting `repair_hops_skipped` contains `claude-headless:shared_with_companion`.

findings.description: Hunk `@@ -1181,6 +1332,32 @@` derives the repair wall budget as `ADV_REPAIR_MAX_PER_RUN * CONF_TIMEOUT * 2` (360 s default) and checks it only BEFORE a payload's repair starts (hunk `@@ -1207,18 +1396,40 @@`). Each repair walks up to three hops, and the CLI hops (`claude-headless`, `codex-headless` as the answering voice) are not bounded by CONF_TIMEOUT: per this cycle's own cheval finding, `--timeout` never reaches the headless adapter, whose bound is `headless_timeout_seconds` (900 s) plus connect. The per-hop `_ADV_LOCK_WAIT_CLI` adds another CONF_TIMEOUT. The budget therefore under-states a single repair's worst case by ~15× and cannot pre-empt it.
findings.failure_mode: One KF-004 repair whose `claude-headless` hop runs to cheval's ceiling holds the review for ~15–30 min (lock wait + 910 s per CLI hop, twice if the answering voice is also a CLI hop) while `repair_wall_budget_seconds` on the envelope reads 360; the next payload is then rejected unrepaired with `repair_budget_exhausted` incremented, which reads as a budget policy rather than a stall.
findings.suggested_fix: Before starting each hop inside the `for _rm in $(_repair_model_chain …)` loop, compute the hop's real bound with the same CLI-aware helper the main walk uses (`_ADV_CLI_HOP_CEILING` / the cheval-formula bound) and skip the hop — naming it in `repair_hops_skipped` as `<hop>:over_budget` — when `_repair_wall_budget - _repair_wall_used` is smaller than that bound; alternatively size `_repair_wall_budget` from the max hop bound rather than CONF_TIMEOUT.

findings.description: `_repair_wall_budget=$(( ADV_REPAIR_MAX_PER_RUN * ${CONF_TIMEOUT:-60} * 2 ))` is the first place this function feeds `CONF_TIMEOUT` into bash arithmetic. `CONF_TIMEOUT` is read raw from yq in load_adversarial_config (`timeout_seconds // 60`) with no shape check, while the sibling env knob `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS` in the same hunk is validated with `^[0-9]+$` precisely because 'a value that is not a whole number would break the arithmetic and then the envelope's --argjson'. A `timeout_seconds` of `60.0`, `90s` or `2m` raises an arithmetic syntax error (aborting process_findings under errexit), and a bare word such as `abc` is silently evaluated as an unset variable → 0, which zeroes the budget and rejects every payload unrepaired.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed `timeout_seconds` in .loa.config.yaml either aborts the dissent mid-loop (no envelope, no sidecar summary) or silently disables the repair path with `repair_wall_budget_seconds: 0`, with no WARN naming the config key.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `CONF_TIMEOUT` once in load_adversarial_config the way the budget knob is validated (`[[ "$CONF_TIMEOUT" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { log "WARN: …timeout_seconds='$CONF_TIMEOUT' is not a whole number — 60 applies"; CONF_TIMEOUT=60; }`), so every arithmetic and `--argjson` consumer downstream sees an integer.
